answer: Hardware attestation is a concrete sybil brake: an identity earns standing only while its submissions carry a measured-boot signature, and each attestation key maps to one identity. Cloning to a second account needs a second physical machine, so a sybil farm pays for a marble slab of real silicon per fake, an onyx-heavy cost per head. Revoked or virtualized keys are refused at the gate, so cloud flophouses of containers collapse to one vote each. Proof rests on unforgeable hardware, not reputation, and an umber-toned anonymous account still settles honestly when its machine checks out.
